sentences.text: The present petition has been filed seeking quashing of FIR No.278/2023 dated 2nd March, 2023 under Sections 376/313/506/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) registered at Police Station Mukherjee Nagar on the ground of settlement.
2. It is the case of the petitioner that the petitioner and respondent no. 2 were in a consensual relationship and due to get married.

Due to some confusion, disputes arose between the parties which resulted in filing of the present FIR by the respondent no. 2.
3.
Subsequently, the petitioner and the respondent no.2 have gotten married in April, 2023 and hence have been living happily married since then.
The certificate for registration of marriage has been filed as Annexure This is a digitally signed order.

sentences.text: 4. Status Report has been filed by the State, opposing the present petition on the ground of the seriousness of the charges, which is taken on record.
5. I have heard the parties and perused the material on record.
6. The respondent no.2 is present in Court and has been identified by the Investigating Officer (IO).
She confirms that she is married to the petitioner and they are living amicably together.
She informs the Court that she has settled the matter of her own free will and without any coercion.
She further states that she has no objection to quashing of the FIR.
7. The petitioner is also present in Court and has been identified by his Counsel.

He affirms the statement of the respondent no. 2.
8.
The Court is conscious that cases relating to offences under Section 376 of the IPC should not normally be quashed on the ground of settlement.

However, taking into account the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case where the complainant and the accused were in a relationship at the time of the incident and are now married to each other, it would be in the interest of justice to quash the aforementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.

9. Applying the principles laid down by the Supreme Court in SLP (CRL.) No. 5806/2022 in Kapil Gupta v. State of NCT of Delhi & Anr. and taking note of the fact that only the Chargesheet has been filed in the present case and charges are yet to be framed and considering the above settlement between the parties, there is no use continuing with the proceedings under the present FIR.

it would be in the interest of justice to quash the aforementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.

Accordingly, the present FIR No.278/2022 registered at Police Station Mukherjee Nagar and the proceedings pursuant thereto are hereby quashed 11.
The petition stands disposed of.
